1.explanation: In Carbon v7.48.0, the TableHeader component destructures `...rest` and then places it on the `<th>` only when `isSortable` is false (around line 74). For the sortable variant, it wraps the header label in a `<button>` but mistakenly spreads `...rest` onto that `<button>` (around line 116) instead of the outer `<th>`. By passing a custom `id` (or any other prop) via `getHeaderProps` on a sortable header, you can see that the `id` ends up on the button rather than the TH, reproducing the bug. This minimal example shows exactly that behavior.
1.bug_scenario: When you render a sortable column header via the `TableHeader` component and pass arbitrary props (for example, an `id` to satisfy WCAG H43 “use id/headers”), those props are being spread onto the inner `<button>` element, not onto the `<th>` itself. That means your `<th>` has no `id`, and all of your rest-props (like `id`, `data-*`, etc.) end up on the button instead. In contrast, non-sortable headers correctly spread those props on the `<th>`.
